relationship.statement: For small angles, a pendulum's period depends only on its length and gravity, not on its mass or release angle. Longer pendulums swing slower.
assumptions: The string is massless and does not stretch.
Air resistance and pivot friction are negligible.
Release angles are small enough that sin(θ) ≈ θ.

quantities.label: Length
quantities.meaning: Distance from the pivot point to the center of the bob.

quantities.label: Bob mass
quantities.meaning: Mass of the weight at the end of the pendulum.

quantities.label: Release angle
quantities.meaning: Starting angle from vertical before the pendulum is released.

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Gravitational acceleration pulling the bob downward (9.81 m/s^2 on Earth).

quantities.label: Period
quantities.meaning: Time taken to complete one full back-and-forth swing.

quantities.label: Frequency
quantities.meaning: Number of complete swings per second.

quantities.label: Max speed
quantities.meaning: Peak speed of the bob as it passes through the lowest point.

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { const g = 9.81; const theta0 = 15 * Math.PI / 180; const L = inputs.L; const m = inputs.m; const T = 2 * Math.PI * Math.sqrt(L / g); const f = 1 / T; const omega = 2 * Math.PI / T; const theta = theta0 * Math.cos(omega * t); const theta_deg = theta * 180 / Math.PI; const v_max = omega * L * theta0; const x = L * Math.sin(theta); const y = -L * Math.cos(theta); const v_tan = -L * omega * theta0 * Math.sin(omega * t); const vx_end = x + 0.3 * v_tan * Math.cos(theta); const vy_end = y + 0.3 * v_tan * Math.sin(theta); const bobSize = 0.25 + 0.75 * ((m - 0.5) / 4.5); return { T, f, v_max, theta_deg, x, y, vx_end, vy_end, bobSize, isShort: L < 0.8, isLong: L > 1.4 }; }

outputs.meaning: Time taken to complete one full back-and-forth swing.
Number of complete swings per second.
Peak speed of the bob at the lowest point.
Current angle of the pendulum from vertical in degrees.
X-coordinate of the velocity arrow tip.
Y-coordinate of the velocity arrow tip.
Normalized visual size of the bob based on mass.
True when the pendulum length is short.
True when the pendulum length is long.

always: Period depends on length, not mass.

cases.text: Short string: fast swing, low T.
Long string: slow swing, high T.

lesson.title: What changes a pendulum's swing?
lesson.description: Watch a pendulum swing back and forth as you adjust its length and bob mass. Compare the motion and angle graph to see what actually changes the period.
lesson.instructions: Use the Length slider to make the string shorter or longer, and the Bob mass slider to change the weight. Watch the period, frequency, and angle graph.
lesson.goal: A pendulum's period depends only on its length and gravity, not on its mass.
